answer: Epoch history match rule. At each boundary, every identity submits a cipher digest of its recent actions; it must match its prior two epoch digests within a fixed tolerance or rewards freeze for audit. A sybil must therefore sustain 12 distinct valid actions per epoch for 6 epochs per identity, because shared histories fail the match. An attacker pays that full action cost for every copy plus an audit fee per mismatch. A grove cluster applies the same checks. A tundra cluster does too.
